newsitem.title: USA: No conclusion yet on Saudi blast - Clinton.
newsitem.headline: No conclusion yet on Saudi blast - Clinton.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday he had not reached a conclusion on responsibility for a truck bomb blast that killed 19 U.S. troops in Saudi Arabia.

"I think it is only fair to say ... the investigation is not completed. I have not been presented with any final conclusions," he said when asked by reporters if he had any evidence to support reports the Saudis were convinced Iran had supported the June attack at a military complex in Dhahran.

"I have not reached any final conclusions myself and because of that anything I say about what we do if we knew what had happened would only give rise to an inference that I had really concluded someone was guilty of something that I don't know they are guilty of yet," Clinton said.
"So I can't say more except to say that we are on top of this and we are going to stay on top of it," he added at a White House news conference.
Iran has denied any connection with the blast.

Following recent broadcast and published reports that the Saudis had told FBI Director Louis Freeh they believed the attack was carried out by Saudi extremists with the backing of Iran, the Los Angeles Times reported this week that Washington was making contingency plans for possible retaliation, including military strikes, against Iran.
